Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `fix-opengl-performance-tests`, not initiated by that change.

- **GoogleTest goto-error false candidate**: `Tests/src/...` compiled headers emit `if (size == -1l) goto error;` (3211) warnings from vendored code — cosmetic.
  **id:** §1 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Pango shaping vs. FreeType per-character measurement**: pango applies shaping/rounding (e.g. alternate glyph for digits), so individual glyph boxes can differ between the FreeType reference in `TextMetricsAll` and the Pango backends for the same codepoint; `TextMetricsCairoTest` and `TextMetricsSVGTest` tolerate this via margins.
  **id:** §2 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Open items of the SVG text metrics work (implemented by `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-12-fix-text-metrics-consistency`).

- **Approximation fallback in builds without pango and without FreeType**: such a build cannot measure real font metrics, so the `text-metrics-consistency` requirement "the non-Pango variant SHALL measure with real font metrics" holds only where FreeType is available; there the backend keeps the character count approximation (glyph `width`/`height` are set, not uninitialized) and logs a warning. Scoping the requirement accordingly was deliberately left as this note instead of a spec change or a follow-up change.
  **id:** §3 · **category:** docs-and-specs · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold spec scoping
- **Label rectangle vs. union of glyph boxes (pango SVG path)**: the pango build of the SVG backend reports a label width that deviates from the union of its per-glyph ink boxes by ~1.2 px (pango derives the label ink extents from its own shaping), slightly above the 1 px tolerance of the `text-metrics-api` scenario; `TextMetricsSVGTest` allows 2 px there. Pre-existing, the pango path was not changed.
  **id:** §4 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Pre-existing issues found during `fix-text-metrics-shields`.

Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `map-painter-visible-object-cull`, not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

- **The label layouter's viewport belongs to the previous frame in the early render steps**: a backend reports the viewport of a frame from its drawing target in `BeforeDrawingCallback` (the `Prerender` step 7, for example `MapPainterCairo.cpp:700`), while the way shield labels are registered in step 3, in front of it. A label decision taken in the early steps therefore sees the viewport of the previous frame (or an empty one in the first frame). The change handles this by only deciding a label when the viewport of the frame has been reported (`SetViewport` marks it, `Reset` clears the mark), so the shield labels of a frame are not decided by the shared label stage; their rejection happens in the painter, which uses the projection. A cleaner arrangement would report the viewport at the start of a frame (the painter's `InitializeRender`) from the drawing target, but the viewport of a tiled backend is the rectangle of the target within the surface and only the backend knows it.
  **id:** §5 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Way line style resolution has no observation hook for tests**: `MapParameter::RegisterFillStyleProcessor` makes the per-ring fill style resolution of the area path observable, but there is no counterpart for the line styles of a way. The unit tests of the way rejection can therefore only guard the contract (a way outside the view adds no prepared way, no coordinates and no shield label) and its regression properties; that the early rejection *removes work* is verified by the before/after measurement of the step (`map-painter-visible-object-cull`, `verification.md`) instead. A line style processor would close that gap.
  **id:** §7 · **category:** tests-and-harness · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Pre-existing issues found during import-performance analysis of the `further-types-styles-symbols-and-fixes` branch (671 -> 1527 types). Process in separate changes.

- **Uncrustify conformance drift in map backends**: `libosmscout-map-skia/src/osmscoutmapskia/MapPainterSkia.cpp`, `libosmscout-map-qt/src/osmscoutmapqt/MapPainterQt.cpp` and `libosmscout-map-svg/{src/osmscoutmapsvg/MapPainterSVG.cpp,include/osmscoutmapsvg/MapPainterSVG.h}` (also `MapPainterCairo.*` include) are widely unformatted w.r.t. the `.uncrustify` config (brace style, alignment), pre-dating `fix-text-metrics-shields`; new code follows the file-local style and is uncrustify-clean where added. Consider a file-wide formatting pass in a dedicated change.
  **id:** §8 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Issues found during analysis of the `further-types-styles-symbols-and-fixes` branch (PR #1782, 671 -> 1527 types), covering import speed, database size, data loading speed and rendering speed. Process in separate changes.
- **PBF reader drops unregistered tags**: `PreprocessPBF.cpp:312` (`if (id!=tagIgnore)`) discards tags not registered in the type definition. This means no-match objects in real imports are those with registered keys but non-matching values (e.g. `highway=foobar`), not arbitrary unknown tags. Affects how no-match cost should be estimated; also means `source`/`note`-only objects take the empty-tag fast path.
  **id:** §9 · **category:** import · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **Micro-benchmark underestimates import type-resolution cost ~2-3x**: `Tests/src/TypeResolutionPerformanceTest.cpp` (new) measures per-call cost with hot cache; import measurements (cold cache, tagMap construction, string compares on hits) are ~2-3x higher per call. Use import-level measurements as ground truth.
  **id:** §10 · **category:** import · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **Type ID byte width is unchanged by this branch**: measured by running `Tests/src/TypeResolutionPerformanceTest.cpp` against both type definition files (with the #1787 code), both report `Type ID bytes: node 2, way 1, area 2`. The master type set already has 335 node types and 444 area types and therefore already exceeds the 1-byte range (node ids up to 334, area ids up to 443), so the growth 671 -> 1527 types (854 node, 192 way, 1097 area) causes no size or read cost change in `nodes.dat`/`ways.dat`/`areas.dat` or the raw files.
  **id:** §11 · **category:** database · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **Geometry-aware way/area resolution split**: with the tag-key dispatch index in place the remaining import win is geometry: an open way never needs area resolution and a closed way never needs way resolution unless its type sets `PinWay` (`TypeInfo::IsPinWay()`). `Preprocess.cpp:337` resolves both in one `GetWayAreaType` pass and knows the geometry before it does. Not implemented.
  **id:** §12 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold way/area resolution semantics
  - **Loop verdict**: measured 2026-10-16T10:41:11Z against `stylesheets/map.ost` and the 20000 tag maps of `Tests/src/TypeResolutionTest.cpp`: searching only the geometry-appropriate kind changes the resolved way type for 88/20000 and the resolved area type for 156/20000 tag maps, so the premise "an open way never needs area resolution" does not hold. `TypeConfig::GetWayAreaType` (`libosmscout/src/osmscout/TypeConfig.cpp:1259-1294`) returns the single first satisfied condition in type-definition order and assigns only the geometry kinds that condition's mask covers, so the area kind feeds the way result and the two "Should be way/area …" diagnostics of `Preprocess.cpp:379-385`, `:406-411` exist for exactly this case. Witness: `{building=bakery, barrier=fence, power=pedestrian}` resolves to `wayType=ignore` (masked by `TYPE shop = NODE AREA (EXISTS "shop")`, `map.ost:6319`) where the way-only search finds `barrier_fence` (`map.ost:8670` vs `:8690`). The measurement case was reverted and the number is **not retained in the repo**; it was obtained by running the temporary case against the corpus above, and the run log and provenance sit machine-locally in `.pi/bugfix-loop/evidence/s12-geometry-split-measurement-2026-10-16T104111Z.log` with `s12-geometry-split-provenance-2026-10-16.txt`. Decision owed: may way/area resolution become a per-kind first-match search, accepting the type change for ~1.2 % of tag maps and giving up the two "Should be …" diagnostics?
- **Conditions without a declared value still scale with the number of such conditions on one key**: the value-discriminated index of `fix-type-resolution-type-count-cost` only moves conditions that report an exhaustive `(key,value)` set into a value bucket; `TagExistsCondition`, ordering comparisons, negations and numeric equalities stay in the key-level list (`TypeConfig::TypeKeyIndex::keyOnly`) and are evaluated for every object that carries the key. A key on which many types declare such conditions therefore still grows with the type set. The parked type set can be re-enabled once the exact-value conditions are addressed, but this residual has to be re-measured when new types introduce value-less conditions on a crowded key.
  **id:** §14 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold unpark decision
- **Import cost is driven by object count, not by type resolution**: the baseline profile in `maps/Dortmund.txt` (master type set, 28.5 s total) is dominated by `OptimizeAreaWayIds` 10.7 s (37.6%), `CoordData` 4.2 s, `WayAreaData` 3.2 s, `Preprocess` 2.6 s (9.1%), `MergeAreas` 1.5 s, `WayWayData` 1.0 s and `RouteData` 0.9 s; every remaining step is below 0.8 s. That extract produces 349,965 areas, 78,792 ways, 43,074 nodes and 2,303,922 coordinates, and every step above is O(objects) (or O(areas log areas)). The branch adds 860 types (617 non-`_building` types, 243 new `_building` variants, 9 removed) whose node/area capability directly raises those counts. Resolution is ~9% of the import and only part of it doubles, so the object growth is the term to measure, not the resolution.
  **id:** §15 · **category:** import · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **A/B import measurement harness is missing**: import a fixed extract (`maps/Dortmund.osm.pbf`, 20 MB) twice with the same binary, once with the master `map.ost` and once with the branch `map.ost`, then compare per-step timings from the import log, per-file byte sizes, `stats.dot` and the object counts. Without this, every statement about import time and database size growth in this list stays qualitative.
  **id:** §16 · **category:** tests-and-harness · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **`AreaIndexGenerator` allocates per-type containers per magnification level**: `libosmscout-import/include/osmscoutimport/AreaIndexGenerator.h:435` builds `std::vector<CoordOffsetsMap> typeCellOffsets(typeConfig->GetTypeCount())` and `:540` builds `std::vector<CoordCountMap> cellFillCount(typeConfig.GetTypeCount())` inside the level loop, so 1097 empty `std::map`s are constructed per level, most of which stay empty. Size these to the types actually indexed at that level, or key them by type index in an `unordered_map`. In addition `CalculateDistribution` emits one `progress.Info` per type per level (`:594`) and `WriteBitmap` one per type, so the import log grows with the type count (`maps/Dortmund.txt` is 284 KB with 444 area types).
  **id:** §17 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Database size is bounded by `coord.dat`, which the type set does not affect**: in `maps/Dortmund`, `coord.dat` is 875,139,156 bytes of the 874 MB total (99.9%), and `GenCoordDat` writes every raw coordinate of the input (2,303,922 for Dortmund) independently of the type definition. What does grow: `types.dat` (44 KB -> ~100 KB at ~66 B/type), `distribution.dat` (12 B/type), the per-type area tile bitmaps in `areaarea.idx`/`areaway.idx`/`areanode.idx` (+675 area types, mostly sparse), `areaaddress.dat` (`ADDRESS` types 305 -> 880) and the location/POI indexes (`location*`, `textloc.dat`, `textpoi.dat`; `POI` types 5 -> 54, i.e. 10.8x). Mitigating: `AreaAreaIndexGenerator`'s `AreaLocationProcessorFilter` unsets the `Location` and `PostalCode` feature values before the data is written to disk, so enabling `ADDRESS`/`POI` on more types costs index entries rather than per-object feature bytes. Net effect on a whole database is expected to be a few percent.
  **id:** §19 · **category:** database · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **No backend caches rendered symbols**: `MapPainterCairo.cpp:1203`, `MapPainterQt.cpp:700`, `MapPainterAgg.cpp:489` and `MapPainterSVG.cpp:1094` construct a renderer and replay `Symbol::GetPrimitives()` on every draw. Symbols grew 108 -> 433 and their drawing primitives 207 -> 1314, and symbol-based icons (`AREA.ICON`) 10 -> 112 selectors, so per-frame symbol cost grew by an order of magnitude. Icons are already cached (`MapPainterCairo.cpp:471` `HasIcon`, `MapPainterQt.cpp:685` -> `images`), and `libosmscout-client-qt/src/osmscoutclientqt/IconLookup.cpp` already rasterizes symbols into cached pixmaps for hit-testing. A raster cache in `DrawSymbol` keyed by symbol and quantized scale factor is the largest single rendering win; path-following symbol draws (`MapPainterQt.cpp:660`, `DrawContourSymbol`) need a bypass or a rotation-aware cache. Correction by `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-26-map-painter-label-reuse`: the allocation share of the `DrawLabels` step is not the symbol drawing but the layouter's overlap resolution (at zoom 15, 1988 of the step's 2012 allocations per frame belong to the layouter, and 24 to drawing), so this item is a frame-time item, not an allocation item.
  **id:** §21 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **243 new `_building` types duplicate their non-building twin in the stylesheets**: the branch defines both `shop_supermarket` and `shop_supermarket_building` and always styles them together (`stylesheets/include/shop.oss:778` `[TYPE shop_supermarket, shop_supermarket_building]`). Folding each pair into one type plus a geometry-specific style would remove ~16% of the type set, which helps resolution candidate sets, `TypeInfoSet` size, `types.dat`, `distribution.dat` and the area index tables at the same time. This changes type ids and therefore needs a database format decision, so it is recorded here rather than recommended.
  **id:** §23 · **category:** type-definitions · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold database format
- **`AreaData::clippings` is still a `std::list<CoordBufferRange>`**: `libosmscout-map/include/osmscoutmap/MapPainter.h:255`, read directly by GDI, AGG, Cairo, Skia, DirectX, SVG and the Android JNI painter, so a contiguous store touches six backends. The prepared store conversion (`map-painter-frame-containers`) and the area preparation scratch reuse (`map-painter-area-preparation`) both left it out.
  **id:** §25 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The label stage still copies per label and per frame**: `LabelLayouter::DrawLabels` collects the postponed text and overlay elements into two `std::vector<const Element*>` per frame (`libosmscout-map/include/osmscoutmap/LabelLayouter.h:868-869`, 24 allocations per frame on the fixed view at zoom 15); the label data is copied into the resolved label instances; the measurement key of a label whose text exceeds the small-string buffer allocates its string buffer; and `LabelLayouter::MeasurementOrder` holds a second copy of that key. Reused layouter members, an intrusive order list, or an order list of pointers into the index would drop them.
  **id:** §26 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The IOS backend keys its font cache by size alone as well**: `libosmscout-map-iosx/include/osmscoutmapiosx/MapPainterIOS.h:170` (`std::map<size_t,Font*> fonts`) resolves the family from `parameter.GetFontName()` (`MapPainterIOS.mm:67`) but keys the cache by the scaled font size, so a painter kept open across a font-name change keeps serving the font of the earlier name - the same defect `fix-font-cache-key` fixed for the Cairo and SVG backends. It needs an Apple run to verify, which is why it was left out of that change; the SVG backend's pango-less face cache (`MapPainterSVG::GetFontFace`, `fontFaces` keyed by font file and pixel size) was already correct and was not part of the defect.
  **id:** §28 · **category:** apple · **class:** bug · **status:** open (platform)
- **GDI+ text metrics depend on the device context resolution**: `libosmscout-map-gdi` measures through `Gdiplus::Font` and the `HDC` of the render target (`MapPainterGDI.cpp:272`, `:387`), so its measurement environment also depends on the resolution of the device context, not only on the projection. The label reuse of `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-26-map-painter-label-reuse` sets the environment from the font name, the font size factor, the DPI and the magnification of the projection (`MapPainterGDI::DrawMap`), which covers the projection but not an application that switches between device contexts of different resolutions while keeping one painter and one projection.
  **id:** §29 · **category:** windows · **class:** bug · **status:** open (platform)
- **Icons and patterns load lazily while painting, there is no preload step**: `MapPainterCairo::HasIcon` (`libosmscout-map-cairo/src/osmscoutmapcairo/MapPainterCairo.cpp:471`) and `HasPattern` (`:515`) as well as `MapPainterQt::HasIcon` (`libosmscout-map-qt/src/osmscoutmapqt/MapPainterQt.cpp:84`) decode the PNG on the first draw that needs it, and no `GetIconNames`/`LoadIcon` preload API could be found. With icons, patterns (~4 -> ~25) and symbols (108 -> 433) grown, the first frames after a style switch or a pan that reveals a new type pay those decodes. `StyleConfig` already exposes the name lists (`GetSymbolNames`, `GetPatternNames`), so a preload pass is available. Related: `MapPainterQt.h:81` resolves icons through `std::map<std::string,QImage,std::less<>>`, i.e. a string-keyed lookup per icon draw, where `MapPainterCairo.h:92` uses a `std::vector<cairo_surface_t*>` indexed by `GetIconId()`. Low impact today because the branch moved to symbols (573 vs 137 `ICON { symbol: ... }` uses, only about 7 `name:`-style left), but any future `name:`-based icon pays the string lookup.
  **id:** §30 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Object caches are sized in object counts, so the new types degrade the hit rate**: `libosmscout/include/osmscout/db/Database.h:85-90` defaults to `nodeDataCacheSize=5000`, `wayDataCacheSize=40000`, `areaDataCacheSize=5000`, `areaAreaIndexCacheSize=5000`, `routeDataCacheSize=1500`. Those sizes are independent of the type set, but the per-tile working set grows with the new types, so a viewport touches proportionally more distinct objects than the cache holds. Related: `DataFile::GetByOffset(..., boundingBox, ...)` (`libosmscout/include/osmscout/io/DataFile.h`) reads all candidate offsets and only then filters by bounding box, warning below a 50% hit rate, so more area types means more requested offsets and more discarded reads.
  **id:** §31 · **category:** client-data · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Two more per-type container allocations in the import generators**: `libosmscout-import/src/osmscoutimport/GenWayWayDat.cpp:823` allocates `std::vector<std::list<RawWayRef>> waysByType(typeConfig->GetTypeCount())`, and `libosmscout-import/src/osmscoutimport/GenMergeAreas.cpp:475` allocates `std::vector<AreaMergeJob> mergeJobs(typeConfig.GetTypeCount())` (looping all types again at `:477` and `:778`). Both are 2.3x bigger with 1527 types, and `GenWayWayDat` additionally walks all type ids twice (`:844`, `:891`) with a `progress.Info` per type at `:899`.
  **id:** §32 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** open (needs a test seam for the container sizes — the count is the element count of two function-local containers)
  - **Loop verdict**: confirmed 2026-10-16T11:02:51Z — both allocations and all three walks hold at `GenWayWayDat.cpp:823`/`:844`/`:891` and `GenMergeAreas.cpp:475`/`:477`, and 1527/671 defined types is the 2.28x the entry claims (the `:472` citation is the allocation at `:475` today). Skipped as `needs-device`: the delta changes the size of two function-local vectors only, so the count it would have to assert — slots allocated, or defined type ids walked — has no host seam. There is no accessor for either container, and a walk over a type that has no work calls nothing on `Progress`, so a test-local `Progress` subclass cannot count it; an accessor or a counter would be a production addition beyond the delta. The item stays an open improvement: the produced files cannot change, so it is memory-only and the loop's red-case rule (condition 7) cannot pin it.
- **The Qt font cache stated no identity rule and was never released**: the size a cached font is selected by is a `size_t` field, `FontDescriptor::fontSize` (`libosmscout-map-qt/include/osmscoutmapqt/MapPainterQt.h:62-73`), while the value assigned to it at `MapPainterQt.cpp:66` is the `double` product of the label size with `projection.ConvertWidthToPixel(parameter.GetFontSize())`; the truncation that follows is what keeps the number of distinct identities at the number of distinct pixel sizes on screen. That is why the recorded claim that auto-sized labels "miss the cache every time" does not hold for Qt: `MapPainter::LayoutPointLabels` (`libosmscout-map/src/osmscoutmap/MapPainter.cpp:445-466`) does produce a continuum of sizes, and the truncation collapses it to the pixel grid. What did hold is the missing release: the destructor carried `// TODO: Clean up fonts` (`MapPainterQt.cpp:55-59`) and never cleared the cache, while `StyleSheetChanged` (`:886-891`) already dropped the pattern images of a replaced stylesheet. Both the identity rule and the release are addressed by `qt-font-cache-identity-and-release`; the other backends are recorded in §95.
  **id:** §33 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** bug · **status:** open (PR #1873)
- **`AreaIndexGenerator::MakeAreaIndex` reads the whole object file once per magnification level, twice**: `libosmscout-import/include/osmscoutimport/AreaIndexGenerator.h:536-569` (`CalculateDistribution`) does `scanner.GotoBegin()` and parses every object once per level, and the write phase repeats that (`:416-458`, `scanner.GotoBegin()` inside the `for (l=areaIndexMinMag; l <= maxLevel; l++)` loop). With the defaults `areaWayIndexMinMag=10` and `areaWayIndexMaxMag=15` (`libosmscout-import/src/osmscoutimport/ImportParameter.cpp:88-91`) that is up to 6 levels x 2 = ~12 full reads of `ways.dat` for the area-way index alone. This is the one import stage found so far that genuinely scales with the type count: the loop condition is `!remainingObjectTypes.Empty()`, so more types that need a coarser index level mean more iterations, each a full file scan. Cost is low at Dortmund scale (0.337 s, `ways.dat` is 2.9 MB) but linear in file size.
  **id:** §35 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold single-pass memory bound
  - **Loop verdict**: confirmed 2026-10-16T10:45Z — the step parses 14000 objects for 2000 objects over the default range, i.e. six distribution parses plus one write parse (`Tests/src/AreaIndexSinglePassTest.cpp`, reverted; run log **not retained in the repo**, obtained as `openspec/changes/fix-area-index-single-pass/evidence/red-A-area-index-single-pass.log` before that directory was removed as a phantom change, machine-locally `.pi/bugfix-loop/evidence/s35-red-single-pass-parses-20261016T104503Z.log`), so the entry's claim holds. The delta "one pass per phase" is not reachable without a memory decision, which is why the entry is on hold: the distribution walk counts a level's cells only for the types still remaining (`AreaIndexGenerator.h:557-559`), so a single pass over all levels has to count every type at every level, and the cell maps it would hold grow with the level range. Measured on a fixture at this entry's scale (20 spread types x 5000 ways over 5x5 degrees plus one dense type of 5000 ways, 105000 ways, one type surviving to level 15): a single pass holds 383843 cells over the six levels against the 4644 cells of the current walk's peak (ratio 81, about 20 MiB of `std::map` nodes, `TEMP-REVERT-PROBE`, reverted, log `.pi/bugfix-loop/evidence/s35-single-pass-cell-maps-probe-20261016T104838Z.log`). The write phase alone could be collapsed into one pass with today's memory (each object has exactly one index level), but not the distribution walk. Deriving the coarser levels from the finest one by parent aggregation does not reproduce the counts, because an object whose box spans two children of one parent is counted once by the per-level walk and twice by the aggregation. Decision owed: may the distribution walk hold the cell maps of every level (memory growing with the level range, measured 81x on the fixture above) to remove the up to six re-parses — and if the memory must stay at one level, is the per-level walk to stay as it is?

- **Tile cache memory: 6 `TypeInfoSet` per cached tile, so the type growth alone adds ~8 MB**: `libosmscout-map/include/osmscoutmap/DataTileCache.h:320-410` exposes six `TileData` per tile (node, way, area, route, optimized way, optimized area) and each holds a `TypeInfoSet types` (`:57`). At 671 types that is 6 x 5.4 KB = 32 KB per tile, at 1527 types 6 x 12.2 KB = 73 KB, so the offline tile cache of 200 tiles (`libosmscout-client-qt/include/osmscoutclientqt/OSMScoutQt.h:71-72`) carries about 6.5 MB -> 14.6 MB and the online cache of 100 tiles 3.2 MB -> 7.3 MB of type tables alone, before counting a single object. Aggravating: `GetTypes()` returns the set by value (`DataTileCache.h:212`); `TileData::AddPrefillData` uses the copying overload for the object vector (`this->prefillData=data;`); `ResolveXFromParent` pays a `TypeInfoSet` copy, `Remove`/`Intersects`/`Intersection` over all types, a scan of every parent object and a vector copy, four times per tile; eviction is coarse (`libosmscout-client-qt/src/osmscoutclientqt/TileCache.cpp:201` drops `cacheSize/10` = 20 tiles at once); and every `TileData` carries its own `std::mutex`. The `TypeInfoSet` bitmap change would shrink the per-tile tables from 73 KB to roughly 1.2 KB.
  **id:** §36 · **category:** client-data · **class:** improvement · **status:** fixed-by fix-typeinfoset-bitmap-storage
  - **Loop verdict**: rejected as stale 2026-10-16T11:05:24Z by the run's second pre-screen — `TypeInfoSet` now stores a bit per defined type plus a reference per contained type (`libosmscout/include/osmscout/TypeInfoSet.h:111-119`), so the 73 KB-per-tile premise of this entry no longer holds; the 6 sets per tile remain, but they no longer scale with the type count.
- **Flag deltas that make import stages type-count dependent**: `MERGE_AREAS` 75 -> 122 (+47), `OPTIMIZE_LOW_ZOOM` 54 -> 74 (+20), `MULTIPOLYGON` 7 -> 16 (+9), `IGNORESEALAND` 23 -> 47 (+24). `GenMergeAreas` therefore runs its per-area node-id dedup for 122 types instead of 75 (1.6x) on top of the per-object `unordered_set` noted above, and `OptimizeAreasLowZoom`/`OptimizeWaysLowZoom` iterate 20 more types. The `IGNORESEALAND` delta is a behaviour change rather than a cost one: `GenWaterIndex` reads only that flag (`GenWaterIndex.cpp:251-252`, no per-type loop, bitmaps per magnification level) and excludes those ways from land-mass determination. The new entries are all the new `barrier_*` (`guard_rail`, `kerb`, `jersey_barrier`, `chain`, ...) and `waterway_*` (`drainage_channel`, `fairway`, `fish_pass`, `flowline`, `tidal_channel`, ...) types plus `place_sea` - worth checking whether newly flagging `place_sea` shifts land/sea resolution near coasts.
  **id:** §38 · **category:** import · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold unpark decision

Priority by axis, largest lever first:

| axis | lever |
|------|-------|
| render | raster symbol cache; icon/pattern preload; remaining label-stage scratch (per-frame pointer vectors, measurement-key copies) |
| data loading | `TypeInfoSet` as a bitmap (also 6 sets per cached tile); per-tile `TypeInfoSet` copies; location lookup has no region cache |
| render (secondary) | `StyleConfig` type x level tables; missing label cap; font cache keyed by an unquantized `double` |
| import | object count (still unmeasured); per-type container allocations; tag-signature resolution cache; type-count-driven flag deltas (`MERGE_AREAS`, `OPTIMIZE_LOW_ZOOM`) |

Symbol caching helps rendering only; it does not affect data loading, whose per-pan-step cost is dominated by the per-tile `TypeInfoSet` copies.

Issues and follow-ups found during the same PR #1782 analysis, beyond the four performance axes (pattern wiring, client data, packaging, backend coverage, style switching, CI). Process in separate changes.

- **Two new `ADMIN_REGION` types are missing from the client size heuristic and fall back to 2 m**: `place_subcounty` and `place_cadastral_community` are new in this branch (0 -> 1 occurrences each) and both carry `ADMIN_REGION`, but `libosmscout-client-qt/src/osmscoutclientqt/SearchModule.cpp` `UsualObjectSize` has no entry for either, so both hit the `return Meters(2.0);` fallback while neighbouring types get 20-90 km (`place_district` 50 km, `place_subdistrict` 30 km, `place_municipality` 20 km). The branch extended that map for about 15 other new `place_*` types, so this looks like an omission. Affects search-result map zoom and POI size. Also worth deciding about the generic `place_any` and about `place_building_complex` (neither is `ADMIN_REGION`).
  **id:** §50 · **category:** client-qt · **class:** bug · **status:** on-hold unpark decision
- **The AGG backend cannot draw name-based icons, so the remaining `ICON { name: ... }` styles are invisible in AGG consumers such as `StyleEditor`**: `MapPainterAgg::HasIcon` returns `false` (`libosmscout-map-agg/src/osmscoutmapagg/MapPainterAgg.cpp:211-218`) and `MapPainterAgg::DrawIcon` is `// Not implemented` (`:482`). Because `HasIcon` returns false, `MapPainter::LayoutPointLabels` (`libosmscout-map/src/osmscoutmap/MapPainter.cpp:393-422`) falls through to `iconStyle->GetSymbol()`, so the move of 573 icon uses to `symbol:` in this branch actually fixes icons for AGG (symbols are implemented at `:489`). The about 7 remaining `ICON { name: ... }` styles (`bench`, `bus_stop`, `fast_food`, `restaurant`, `start`, `target`, `waste_basket`) stay invisible there; decide whether to convert them to symbols too or to implement `HasIcon`/`DrawIcon` for AGG.
  **id:** §51 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** feature · **status:** open
- **Investigate: no build-system install rule for `libosmscout/data/icons`**. The search over `CMakeLists.txt`, `*.cmake` and `meson.build` finds the icon directories only as test arguments (`Tests/meson.build:538`, `Tests/CMakeLists.txt:308`), so the roughly 20 new pattern PNGs and the four renamed icons (`cemetery.png` -> `landuse_cemetery.png`, `scrub.png` -> `natural_scrub.png`, `forest.png` -> `landuse_forest.png`, `gardenpng` -> `landuse_garden.png`) reach a running app only if the app points at the source tree or ships its own copy. The branch itself is self-consistent (no dangling references to the old file names; only OSM tag values such as `"landuse"=="cemetery"` match), but any out-of-repo theme or icon directory, Android asset copy or iOS bundling step breaks. Audit per platform together with the pattern wiring item above.
  **id:** §52 · **category:** packaging · **class:** feature · **status:** open
- **Investigate: cache invalidation across a style switch (dark mode)**. `IconStyle::GetIconId()` and `FillStyle::GetPatternId()` are assigned per `StyleConfig`, and the caches keyed by them or by icon name live in a long-lived painter (`libosmscout-client-qt/include/osmscoutclientqt/MapRenderer.h:122` `MapPainterQt mapPainter;`, `libosmscout-map-cairo/include/osmscoutmapcairo/MapPainterCairo.h:92-95`). `MapPainterCairo::Close()` destroys the images and patterns and clears the fonts (`MapPainterCairo.cpp:664-687`), but no `Close()` call was found in `TiledMapRenderer`, `MapRenderer` or `DBLoadJob`, so it is unclear whether a style reload invalidates these caches or recreates the painter. With 433 symbols and about 25 patterns this is the first release where a stale id or a stale name-to-surface entry would matter.
  **id:** §53 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** improvement · **status:** unverified
- **Investigate: the per-pan-step dedup cost multiplies with the number of databases**. `libosmscout-client-qt/src/osmscoutclientqt/MapRenderer.cpp:333-353` loops all databases and calls `AddTileDataToMapData` once per database per rebuild (`std::vector<MapData> batch; batch.reserve(databases.size())`), so the six hash maps and the full dedup pass of the perf finding above run per database, not per rebuild, and each database has its own type count (`types.dat`: basemap 768 B, Dortmund 44 KB, NRW 62 KB) so the `TypeInfoSet` sizes differ per database. Measure with the database stack the app actually loads rather than with a single database.
  **id:** §54 · **category:** client-qt · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **Investigate: no CI gate on symbol and pattern consistency**. The branch added `GetSymbolNames()` and `GetPatternNames()` and extended `Demos/src/SymbolsAll.cpp` (which satisfies the `symbol-scan-tool` spec, including `--pattern-path` and a pattern contact sheet, so the tool exists), but nothing fails when a stylesheet references a `SYMBOL` or a `pattern:` that is not defined or has no image. With 433 symbols and about 25 patterns that is now worth a test; `Tests/src/StyleConfigSymbolsTest.cpp` already has the listing harness, so a test asserting that every referenced symbol exists and every pattern name resolves to an image in the standard directory is cheap and would have caught the pattern-wiring and packaging class of problems. (The pattern half is closed by `fix-pattern-path-wiring`: the same test file now resolves the pattern references of all nine shipped stylesheets against `libosmscout/data/icons/14x14/standard` and fails naming the pattern and the stylesheet, verified by removing a referenced image. The symbol half is still unguarded, so the entry stays until that is covered too.)

Negative results for the findings above are collected in the "Checked and found not to be a problem" block of the previous section.

Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `map-painter-area-visibility-cull`, not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

- **Area preparation early-out that no shipped style sheet reaches**: `MapPainter::PrepareAreaRing` returns early when a ring resolves neither a fill nor a border style (`libosmscout-map/src/osmscoutmap/MapPainter.cpp`, the `if (!fillStyle && borderStyles.empty())` test). Measured on the Dortmund database at zoom 15 with `stylesheets/standard.oss`, every ring of every loaded area resolves at least one style, so `styled == rings == 17650` and the early-out is never taken. The check is therefore not dead code in general (a custom style sheet can reach it) but it does not reduce the work of the area preparation step with the shipped style sheets. Not part of `map-painter-area-visibility-cull`, which does not touch it.
  **id:** §56 · **category:** map-rendering · **class:** none · **status:** negative
- **LeakSanitizer reports from fontconfig/pango fail three text-rendering tests in the sanitizer build**: in the `build-asan` configuration documented in AGENTS.md, `ctest --exclude-regex "PerformanceTest"` reports 96 % passed with `MapPainterShieldTest`, `TextMetricsCairoTest` and `TextMetricsSVGTest` failing (`LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks`, for example 65536 bytes in 256 objects). The assertions of all three tests pass; every allocation frame of the report is inside `libfontconfig.so.1` (`FcFontSetList`) or `libpango-1.0.so.0`, reached from the unmodified `MapPainterCairo::Layout`, and no frame is in libosmscout code. With `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0` all three pass. This is the same class of failure that currently excludes `PerformanceTest` from the sanitizer job ("UI libraries leak on exit"). Options: add a LeakSanitizer suppression file for fontconfig/pango, exclude these tests the way `PerformanceTest` is excluded, or set `detect_leaks=0` for them. Not investigated further during `map-painter-area-visibility-cull`, which does not touch text rendering; no pre-change sanitizer build was produced, so their pre-existence rests on the report contents above. Reproduced a second time during `fix-opengl-area-visibility-cull` (94 of 97 tests passed, the same three tests failed, allocation frames dominated by `libpango-1.0`/`libfontconfig`), which reports its run in that change's `verification.md`.
  **id:** §58 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Deferred findings of `publish-container-images`. Process in separate changes.

- **The reported library version carries no commit identity on unreleased builds**: `OSMSCOUT_IMPORT_VERSION` is the library version alone (`Import/CMakeLists.txt:13` from `OSMSCOUT_LIBRARY_VERSION`; `Import/meson.build:6` from `libraryVersion`), so between two milestones a build of the main branch and the last release both report the same version and a generated `db.json` cannot be traced back to the commit that produced it. The version bump pull request makes released artifacts distinguishable from each other (a release asserts that its revision declares the version it publishes), but a database written between releases still cannot be matched to a commit. A `git describe` suffix in the version, or the source revision recorded in the database metadata, would close it; both change what generated metadata records. The query added by the publishing change (`Import --tool-version`) is the only way to read the version out of an image today.
  **id:** §59 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **A version tag does not identify released source in the rolling scheme**: the images are tagged with the release version the source declares, and every later build of the same version overwrites that tag, so only the build stamp identifies released content. A `db.json` in hand cannot be traced back to the exact image that wrote it (only to the milestone). Accepting the scheme was a deliberate decision (design decision 2); an immutable per-release tag - which needs a publication path that does not depend on the release event, see the change's design - would close it.
  **id:** §60 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** on-hold publishing scheme
- **Only `linux/amd64` images are published**: `ghcr.io/framstag/libosmscout/mapgen` and `.../mapserve` are amd64 only - a deliberate scope decision (Non-Goals in the change's design), so an arm64 host still has to build locally. Adding `linux/arm64` means either emulating the build stage (the image compiles the core library and the import library) or a native arm64 runner.
  **id:** §61 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** feature · **status:** on-hold arm64 scope
- **A pinned build expires after the retention window**: the pruning job keeps the newest 20 publications per image and deletes older ones, so a build stamp stops being pullable once that many newer builds exist. A deployment that pins a stamp has to move to a newer one eventually; a longer window is a one-value change (`KEEP_BUILDS` in `.github/workflows/mapgen_image.yml`, repeated in `Documentation/MapRepository.md`).
  **id:** §62 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The version bump is a human step that nothing enforces but the release assertion**: the release workflow cannot write to the main branch (branch protection requires a pull request and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not an admin), so a forgotten bump is caught only when the release is attempted, and until a milestone sets `version:` in `meson.build` the images carry `latest` and the build stamp only. Closing it would need a bypass entry for the Actions app or a PAT secret in the release workflow.
  **id:** §63 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The image build context no longer contains the repository history**: `.dockerignore` excludes `.git/`, which cut the local build context from 107.97 MB to 58.17 MB, but a future build step that reads repository metadata (a version stamp from `git describe`, for example) would now silently see no repository. If such a step is added, drop the `.git/` entry or pass the value in as a build argument instead.
  **id:** §64 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The base images are behind the current releases**: `scripts/mapgen/Dockerfile` builds and runs on `ubuntu:noble` (24.04) and `scripts/mapgen/Dockerfile.serve` serves on `nginx:1.27-alpine`, while Docker Hub carries `ubuntu:26.04` and `nginx:1.31-alpine`. Bumping the distro is not a one-line change: the runtime stage installs from a fixed package list (`libprotobuf32`, `libmarisa0`, `libtbb12`, `libxml2`, `liblzma5`, `libzstd1`, `libgomp1`), which a newer release may rename, and the build stage compiles the import tool against the same distro, so it needs a full image build plus the smoke checks to verify. Not done while the publishing change was prepared: no Docker daemon was reachable on the machine that prepared it. The nginx bump is low risk but equally unverified and belongs in the same change.
  **id:** §65 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **`actions/delete-package-versions@v5` still declares a Node 20 runtime**: it is the current release of that action (checked against `repos/actions/delete-package-versions/releases/latest`), so its two steps keep the runner's `Node 20 is being deprecated` notice even after the other actions in the image workflow were updated to their Node 24 majors. Replacing the two steps with a `gh api` deletion (the API paths are `/users/{owner}/packages/container/{package}/versions`, with the package name URL-encoded) would remove the notice and put the pagination, the retention count and the error handling in our hands.
  **id:** §66 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The compose smoke job pays for a second full image build**: `docker compose -f scripts/mapgen/docker-compose.yml build` does not share the `type=gha` build cache that the `verify` and `publish` jobs use, so that job recompiles the core library and the import library on every run. A `cache_from`/`cache_to` pair on the `mapgen` service would remove most of it; the compose file is otherwise unchanged by `publish-container-images`.
  **id:** §67 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Observations of `mapgen-runtime-identity`.

- **A configured identity has no entry in the image's `/etc/passwd`**: the image's own user is `mapgen` (uid 1000, gid 1000), while `PUID`/`PGID` can name any identity, and a pass then runs without user information: `HOME` is pointed at the writable work area for that reason, and the CI smoke run performs a pass as uid/gid `1234` to show that the pass copes. If a tool turns out to need a passwd entry (locale or user lookups are the usual suspects), the options are to document that the identity has to exist in the image or to add a fallback that maps an unknown uid to the `mapgen` entry. The smoke run is what decides this, so the entry stays until it has passed on a runner.
  **id:** §68 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Conditions of `mapgen-cron-schedule`.

- **The scheduler binary is fetched from GitHub releases at image build time**: `scripts/mapgen/Dockerfile` downloads supercronic (`SUPERCRONIC_VERSION`, v0.2.49) and verifies it against the checksum pinned for the architecture. A build without network access cannot fetch it, and the alternative - vendoring the 14 MB binary into the repository - trades that for a large binary in git. Closing it would need an internal mirror or the binary in the repository.
  **id:** §69 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open
- **The pinned checksums have to be updated with the scheduler**: the version and the two sha256 values (amd64 `a53ae236...`, arm64 `02aa0cb2...`) sit in one `case` block in the same Dockerfile, so an upgrade is a deliberate edit. Nothing checks that the pin matches upstream beyond the build failing if it does not; the arm64 asset is pinned but has never been built or run, because only `linux/amd64` images are published (see the entry above).
  **id:** §70 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Conditions of `mapgen-failure-recovery`.

- **A failing import is visible only in the log and the exit status**: the script now retries and recovers by itself, but in the scheduled mode nobody is told that it keeps failing - supercronic writes the pass output into the container log and moves on. An unattended deployment can fail for weeks without notice. A notification after a failed pass (a webhook, or metrics the operator can alert on) would close it; the pass staying due means the retry itself needs no attention.
  **id:** §71 · **category:** mapgen-container · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Pre-existing issues found while adding the host test for the search scope rule (`test-search-scope-rule`), not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

A better home is `libosmscout-client/` or a core utility location, which would give it the ordinary include path and a module the test can link without JNI; the move touches the JNI bridge's include and both build systems' target definitions and belongs in its own change.

- **Nothing checks that both build systems register the same tests**: a test target has to be declared twice, once in `Tests/CMakeLists.txt` and once in `Tests/meson.build`, and the test name follows a different convention in each (the CMake macro names the test after the target, Meson takes a prose string). A test declared in only one of them is built and run by one build system and silently absent from the other: the `naviveylin-local` branch (PR #1773) registered its new `StringMatcherTest` in CMake only, which is how the gap surfaced. A check comparing the two rosters, or a single list both build systems read, would close it.

Open items of the favorites ordering work (implemented by `openspec/changes/fav-ordering`).

- **Drop the read path for the pre-version favorites file once enough releases have shipped**: `FavoriteLocationService::Load()` still reads the form written before the favorites file carried a format version (groups keyed by name, no stored order, reported sorted by group name) so that upgrading does not lose a user's favorites, and `Documentation/FavoritesFileFormat.md` documents that as a compatibility path with a planned end. Once enough releases have shipped for user files to have been rewritten in the versioned form, that branch can be removed and a version 0 file then handled like any other unsupported version (no groups read, the file never written over). The format version added by that change is what makes the removal decidable without guessing: a version 0 file is identifiable on load, and the removal step has to update the format document and the compatibility table in it in the same move. The version 0 branch is the `LegacyFileFormatVersion` case in `libosmscout-client/src/osmscoutclient/FavoriteLocationService.cpp`.

Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `fix-opengl-area-visibility-cull`, not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

- **An ordinary `Demos/DrawMapAll` run aborts in the heap allocator on a high-DPI view, and no tool reproduces it**: `Demos/DrawMapAll --dpi 300 --width 400 --height 400 --database maps/Dortmund --fontName libosmscout-map-opengl/data/fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf stylesheets/public-transport.oss 51.515 7.465 32768` aborted twice in about forty runs with `Fatal glibc error: malloc.c:3948 (_int_malloc): assertion failed: (unsigned long) (size) >= (unsigned long) (nb)`, on a binary that links neither tcmalloc nor a sanitizer runtime. Tried against it without a reproduction: thirty further runs of the same command, the same command with `--debug`, views of 800x800 and 1200x1200 at the same DPI, `gdb` (which completes the run), `valgrind` (0 errors on the crashing command), and `MALLOC_CHECK_=3` with `MALLOC_PERTURB_=165` over ten runs. No frame of any report is in project code. Whoever picks this up should start from the glibc abort itself rather than from a tool, and should keep the 300 DPI OpenGL view as the trigger to hunt. Found while verifying `fix-opengl-area-visibility-cull`; the reliable failure of the *sanitizer* configuration on the same view was a second allocator interposer and is fixed by `fix-sanitizer-allocator-conflict`.
  **id:** §96 · **category:** apps · **class:** bug · **status:** unverified
- **The OpenGL backend crashes while triangulating a node's geometry, so it cannot render the area-drawing style sheets of the Dortmund database**: `Tests/PerformanceTest --driver opengl` with `maps/Dortmund` and `stylesheets/standard.oss`, `cycle.oss` or `winter-sports.oss` dies with SIGSEGV (exit code 139) at every zoom level and view size tried, down to a single tile at zoom 15. `gdb` places the crash in the vendored triangulator, reached from the node path: `p2t::Sweep::NewFrontTriangle` <- `p2t::Sweep::SweepPoints` <- `p2t::Sweep::Triangulate` <- `osmscout::Triangulate::TriangulatePolygon` <- `osmscout::MapPainterOpenGL::ProcessNode` <- `osmscout::MapPainterOpenGL::ProcessNodes`. `stylesheets/boundaries.oss`, `railways.oss` and `motorways.oss` survive on the same database but load no areas, and only `stylesheets/public-transport.oss` renders areas without crashing (107 to 9646 areas depending on the view), so the OpenGL backend cannot be exercised on that database with the shipped area styles. Reproduced with the source changes of `fix-opengl-area-visibility-cull` stashed, so it predates that change; it is what blocked the rendered viewport-edge comparison of that change (see its `verification.md`).
  **id:** §97 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** bug · **status:** open
- **Every other backend resolves an unquantized font identity and releases it at a different point**: `MapPainterCairo` keys `FontKey{fontName,double fontSize}` (`libosmscout-map-cairo/include/osmscoutmapcairo/MapPainterCairo.h:113-134`) and releases its fonts in `StyleSheetChanged` (`MapPainterCairo.cpp:937-971`) and the destructor; `MapPainterSVG` keys a `PangoFontDescription*` per `FontKey` (`MapPainterSVG.h:89-92`) and frees it only in the destructor (`MapPainterSVG.cpp:138-160`); `MapPainterIOS` keys `std::map<size_t,Font*> fonts` (`MapPainterIOS.h:170`) and releases neither the fonts nor their `Font*` entries (`MapPainterIOS.mm:47-56` frees only the images); `MapPainterDirectX` keys `std::unordered_map<uint32_t,IDWriteTextFormat*>` (`MapPainterDirectX.h:83`) and releases in the destructor and on device loss (`MapPainterDirectX.cpp:1063-1078`); `MapPainterGDI`'s `std::map<FONTDEF,Gdiplus::Font*>` lives in the per-buffer `GdiRender` (`MapPainterGDI.cpp:152`, `:166-179`) and is bounded by that buffer's life; `MapPainterAgg` creates and deletes its font engine inside `DrawMap` (`MapPainterAgg.cpp:754-755`, `:772-773`) but its destructor still carries a stale `// TODO: Clean up fonts` (`:49`). Quantizing the identity to the pixel grid in Cairo and SVG changes the size those backends draw at by less than a device pixel - a rendering change that needs review on a backend that draws fractional font sizes, and their `GetFont` paths are the files of open PR #1871. A cache bound is deliberately not part of this: an LRU bound can release the font a later frame still draws with, which then resolves it again, so the identity rule is what keeps the count small.
  **id:** §95 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `harden-polygon-triangulation`, not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

- **The vendored poly2tri still enforces several invariants with `assert`, which `Release` compiles out**: `libosmscout-map-opengl/src/poly2tri/sweep/advancing_front.cc:85` (`assert(0)`) and the copy's remaining asserts, so a polygon the input validation and the library's own detector both miss is turned into a null dereference in a `Release` build instead of a report. The two input classes the §97 diagnosis found - a ring of fewer than three distinct corners, and a polygon whose sweep loses the triangle of its edge - are covered by the guards added with `harden-polygon-triangulation` (`sweep/sweep.cc` `EdgeEvent`, `common/shapes.cc` `NeighborAcross`, both marked as local deviations from upstream), but any other assert-only invariant still is not. Updating the vendored copy to a revision that reports such input by throwing, or converting the remaining asserts the way the two guards do, closes it; the `Debug` and sanitizer configurations are what keep the asserts active today.
  **id:** §100 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

Pre-existing issues found during implementation of `fix-area-ring-tolerance-all-border-styles`, not initiated by that change. Process in separate changes.

- **The OpenGL area step draws every border style with the width of the first one and applies no border offset**: `MapPainterOpenGL::ProcessAreas` resolves every border style of a ring, but the drawing loop below draws all of them with `borderWidth`, the width of `borderStyles.front()` (`libosmscout-map-opengl/src/osmscoutmapopengl/MapPainterOpenGL.cpp:277`, used at `:390`-`:416`), and that value is `0.0` when the front style carries an offset or a display offset, so a ring whose first border style is offset is drawn with degenerate borders. No border offset is applied anywhere in the library either: `grep -rn "GenerateParallelWay" libosmscout-map-opengl/` finds nothing, while the core painter shifts the ring of each border style before it prepares that style's entry (`MapPainter::PrepareAreaRing`, the `GenerateParallelWay` call above `areaData.push_back`). A style sheet that declares a narrower casing beside a wider line, or a border drawn at an offset, therefore draws differently in this backend than in every other one. Found while widening the visibility tolerance of the backend to the reach of every resolved border style (`fix-area-ring-tolerance-all-border-styles`): that decision is now wider than what the backend draws - conservatively, so no ring is lost - and this drawing defect is what keeps the wider tolerance from showing. A fix needs a rendered comparison, which TODO §97 currently blocks for the Dortmund database.
  **id:** §102 · **category:** map-backend · **class:** bug · **status:** open
- **A CMake toolchain update left `build-asan` unbuildable**: the sanitizer configuration AGENTS.md documents failed with `ninja: error: rebuilding 'build.ninja': subcommand failed` and `/home/tim/.local/share/mise/installs/cmake/latest/cmake-4.4.3-linux-x86_64/bin/cmake: Datei oder Verzeichnis nicht gefunden`, because the directory had been generated by a CMake that a mise update replaced (4.4.3 -> 4.4.4); it had to be re-configured with the documented options before anything could be compiled. A build directory outlives the toolchain that generated it, so a cached sanitizer directory hits this after such an update. Options: re-run the documented configuration (the command `fix-area-ring-tolerance-all-border-styles` recorded in its verification note), or generate the sanitizer build in CI only and never cache it.
  **id:** §103 · **category:** build-and-ci · **class:** improvement · **status:** open

The signature takes the reference non-const (`libosmscout/include/osmscout/db/LocationIndex.h:290`), so a caller such as `libosmscout-client-qt/src/osmscoutclientqt/LookupModule.cpp:471` or the `Demos/src/LocationLookup.cpp:164` consumers can write the `name`, the `parentRegionOffset` or the children of a retained entry, and the next lookup of any other caller of the same index is served the mutated object; `AdminVisitor::Visit(const AdminRegion&)` constrains only the visitor path. No in-tree caller writes. Found while verifying `fix-location-index-region-cache`; the fix is a decision rather than a defect of that change - hand callers a const reference, a copy, or a distinct read-only view - so it stays out of it.
